observations: Photo 0: Front view of a white Canon DSLR camera with a lens attached. The lens cap is black with 'Canon' written on it. The camera body has 'Canon' branding visible. The lens appears to be a standard zoom lens, not a dedicated telephoto or macro lens.
Photo 1: Rear view of the camera showing the LCD screen, control buttons (MENU, INFO, Av, SET, etc.), and the 'Canon' logo on the bezel. The screen is off and reflects the hand holding the camera.

Photo 2: Side view of the camera showing the 'EOS 100D' model name engraved on the body. The lens is attached, and the camera body is white. The lens has a textured grip and a red dot near the front element.
All photos show the camera held in hand, with a tiled floor and metal railing in the background. The watermark 'CDICSON BUSINESS WORLD' is visible on all photos.

claims.claim: The Canon EOS 100D (Rebel SL1) is an ultra-compact, lightweight 18-megapixel APS-C DSLR designed for...
claims.evidence: Photo 2 shows 'EOS 100D' engraved on the camera body, which is the model name. The camera appears compact and lightweight, consistent with the description. The 18-megapixel APS-C sensor is standard for this model, though not visible in photos.

risks.risk: The camera may not power on or function properly (e.g., screen not working, shutter not firing, lens not mounting).
risks.proof: A video showing the camera powering on, the screen turning on, and the shutter firing.

risks.risk: The lens may be damaged or non-functional (e.g., cracked glass, misaligned elements, or missing parts).
risks.proof: Close-up photos of the lens front and rear elements, and a video showing the lens zooming and focusing.

risks.risk: The camera may have internal damage or wear (e.g., sensor scratches, mirror damage, or electronic faults).
risks.proof: A photo of the camera's sensor (if possible) or a video showing the camera in use with clear images.

risks.risk: The camera may be stolen or have a blacklisted serial number.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the serial number on the camera body, and a verification from Canon or a trusted source.

proof_requests: Video showing the camera powering on, screen turning on, and shutter firing.
Close-up photos of the lens front and rear elements.
Photo of the camera's sensor (if possible) or video showing the camera in use with clear images.
Clear photo of the serial number on the camera body.
response.reason: The item is known from the photos. What they cannot prove is priced at its worst case until the proof asked for below arrives.
